title: Generate CHANGELOG release sections at /release from commit bodies instead of hand-editing a shared file
depends_on: none (merge it AFTER the open improve/* branches, which each add a CHANGELOG entry)
brief: MAINTAINER DECISION 18 (2026-09-24): generate the CHANGELOG at /release from commit bodies. Decided: (1) /release compiles the release's section from `git log <previous tag>..HEAD`, keyed on the enforced subject label `<type>(<scope>): vX.Y.Z - <description>` (the commit-subject hook already gates it; `docs/reference/release-process.md` step 6 already selects a release's commits with `git log --grep 'vX.Y.Z - '`); (2) AGENTS.md's 'CHANGELOG.md is updated every session' duty changes (commit bodies become the entries); (3) `.claude/hooks/check-changelog-changed.sh` (a PreToolUse gate that requires a CHANGELOG change on commits touching `.claude/`, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md) is retired or repurposed; (4) the current CHANGELOG.md is archived (the repo already rolls half-years into `docs/changelog-archive/`). FINDING DOCS-L6-07 (lane-6.findings.md:376, verified in the sprint's verify files): 7 of 29 merges carried a resolved CHANGELOG hunk; recorded losses and repairs `dc2d13a5`, `a035a2d3`, `41d4afbe`; three incident-born CHANGELOG rules in `docs/ai-includes/git-and-commits.md:56,60,61`; 545 of 809 commits since 2026-07-01 touch the file (1,759,092 B at b2e387db); since 2026-09-14, 97 `### ` entries against 95 commits, 37 headings literally a commit subject. Options compared in the finding: towncrier fragments vs generation from commits; the decision is generation from commits with a stdlib Python script (no new dependency), run by the /release skill (`.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md`), writing a dated section. Scope the writer must settle from the code: every place that tells an agent to edit CHANGELOG.md (git grep -n -i changelog over AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules, .claude/skills, .claude/agents, docs/ai-includes, .ai), the completion workflow, the ship skill, and the hook. The hook's registration lives in `.claude/settings.json` (PROTECTED): if the plan retires the hook, deleting its registration is a Step 0 for Mike; the alternative (keep the file, change what it checks) must be weighed under simplicity-criterion.md. TDD: the generator script gets pytest/unittest tests in `tools/tests/` (fixture repo or fixture `git log` text: grouping by type, the version label, bodies carried through, commits missing the label listed separately). NOT to decide: rewriting past sections; a player-facing prose layer. Merge note: land after the other improve branches or fold their entries at merge. PROTECTED FILES: `.claude/hooks/config-protection.sh` blocks the Edit and Write tools on any file named `settings.json`, `settings.local.json`, `Directory.Build.props` and on `docs/adrs/*.md` unless a user-approved override exists; on 2026-09-24 the orchestrator's attempt to create that override was refused by the harness's auto-mode classifier, so the executor can NEVER edit these files, not even through a shell command. Any edit to them goes into a 'Step 0: before dispatch (Mike, in an editor)' section with the exact text to insert, and a check command the executor runs in Step 1 (STOP if Step 0 is missing). Base commit for this plan: a39a9c86 (bannerlord-1.5.x; plans record). At a39a9c86 the full suite is 10,313+ passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed (the two live-Armory tests that failed earlier in the sprint pass now). The executor works on its own branch in its own worktree; it never edits E:\repos\TAOM's working tree (another session's uncommitted work is there). Every excerpt must come from the writer's own read at a39a9c86.

title: Amend three architecture rules to match the code: virtual boundary seams, when a service gets an interface, when a patch gets a hook
brief: MAINTAINER DECISION 19 (2026-09-24): amend all three rules. (A) ARCH-05 (lane-2.findings.md:275): ADR-007 gains a 'Protected-virtual boundary seams' exception with conditions: seam signatures use ids and value types only; each seam body is a single engine call or query; the service's interface stays engine-free; a test subclass overrides every seam the tests reach. Evidence: 5 services use the pattern with 97 virtual seam members (RefugeService 39, CampService 32, SupplyOrderService 13, WardenService 10, RuntimeCacheRebuildService 3), each tested by a subclass; `docs/adrs/007-adapter-pattern.md` '## Exceptions' lists only value types and entry points; `.ai/review-reference.md` grades 'ADR-007 (sealed type in service)' CRITICAL; nothing records the pattern. Also add one line to `.ai/review-reference.md` and to the deep-review Standards lens (`.claude/skills/deep-review/lenses/1-standards.md`). Do NOT plan seaming the 15 raw-read services here. (B) ARCH-01 (lane-2.findings.md:36): the interface rule becomes 'every adapter has an interface; a service gets one only when a test fakes it or a second implementation exists'. Evidence: `1-standards.md:13` demands an interface for every service while `.claude/rules/think-before-coding.md:33` forbids single-implementation interfaces; `.claude/agents/feature-builder.md:40,55` scaffolds `I{Name}Service` for every feature; 477 of 495 interfaces have one implementation, 154 are neither adapter nor test seams. Change the lens line, the feature-builder template and think-before-coding (and ADR-002 only if it states the old rule; check). NO bulk deletion of interfaces: deletions happen opportunistically. (C) ARCH-03 (lane-2.findings.md:228): the 'patch to hook interface to service to adapter' rule (AGENTS.md architecture line, `.claude/rules/csharp-patterns.md` if it states it, `.ai/review-reference.md`) becomes 'patch, model or behavior to service (through a hook interface only when the patch needs a narrow seam or a test fake) to adapter'. Evidence: of 217 patch files, 24 use an IOn* hook interface, 113 reach a service directly; none of the 19 IOn* interfaces is faked in tests. Do NOT delete the two pure forwarders here (they fold when next touched). This is a docs and rules change: no C#; verification is `python tools/lint_docs.py --fail-on-drift`, `bash tools/test_hooks.sh` if any rule file a hook reads changes, and greps proving each old sentence is gone and each new one present. The ADR-007 edit is PROTECTED: put it in Step 0 for Mike with the exact text. PROTECTED FILES: `.claude/hooks/config-protection.sh` blocks the Edit and Write tools on any file named `settings.json`, `settings.local.json`, `Directory.Build.props` and on `docs/adrs/*.md` unless a user-approved override exists; on 2026-09-24 the orchestrator's attempt to create that override was refused by the harness's auto-mode classifier, so the executor can NEVER edit these files, not even through a shell command. Any edit to them goes into a 'Step 0: before dispatch (Mike, in an editor)' section with the exact text to insert, and a check command the executor runs in Step 1 (STOP if Step 0 is missing). Base commit for this plan: a39a9c86 (bannerlord-1.5.x; plans record). title: Wire the Order of Battle Auto-Assign button to HeroAutoAssigner instead of a 'Phase-1 stub' message
brief: MAINTAINER DECISION 21 (2026-09-24): wire Auto-Assign (a feature, its own plan); the other unreachable scaffolding is deleted separately (plan 025). FINDING ARCH-02 part 3 (lane-2.findings.md:214): `Main/Features/CompanionTactics/CompanionTacticsIoC.cs:27` registers `IHeroAutoAssigner`/`HeroAutoAssigner` (51 + 17 lines, 93 test lines) and nothing resolves it. The player-facing button is bound (`Main/_Module/GUI/PreFabs/OOBButtonsOverlay.xml:24`, `Command.Click="ExecuteAssignCharacters"`) to `OOBButtonsVM.cs:73-89`, which prints the literal, unlocalized 'Auto-Assign is a Phase-1 stub, feature pending' (with an em dash) since `55950378` (2026-05-07); the comment at `:81-87` records an earlier adversarial-review P2 on it. The writer must read HeroAutoAssigner, its tests and the Order of Battle screen code (TAOM's OOB view model and the vanilla Order of Battle VM it extends: verify signatures with `pwsh tools/taom-src.ps1 path <Type>`, never guess) and specify: what Auto-Assign does for the player (which heroes go to which formations, respecting what vanilla's own assign logic already does, if any), where the call happens (ADR-002 thin entry: the VM command delegates to the service), co-op gating if the OOB screen runs for a client (check `docs/features/coop-interop.md`), localization of every new player-facing string ({=KEY}default, registered, then translated by the maintainer's pipeline), the feature doc update (`docs/features/` for CompanionTactics or formation presets) and the feature-map row. TDD for the service wiring and the VM command's delegation. In-game check owed (open the Order of Battle before a field battle, press Auto-Assign). If HeroAutoAssigner turns out incomplete or wrong for the current OOB model, the plan says so and specifies the minimum to make it correct; if that exceeds a plan of this size, STOP and say so in the plan's Status instead of inventing a design. Base commit for this plan: a39a9c86 (bannerlord-1.5.x; plans record). brief: MAINTAINER DECISION 21 (2026-09-24): still delete the other unreachable scaffolding (ARCH-02) while Auto-Assign is wired separately (plan 022; do NOT touch HeroAutoAssigner, OOBButtonsVM or CompanionTacticsIoC here).
